description: Add core application features: authentication, dashboard, settings, API routes, dark mode, search, notifications, and profile page.
non_goals: Third-party OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, etc.) — only email/password auth
Real-time WebSocket connections for notifications (polling or static is fine)
Database migrations beyond what the chosen ORM generates automatically

userStories.title: Authentication page with login and signup
userStories.description: Create a combined auth page at /auth with login and signup forms. Include client-side validation, error display, and redirect to /dashboard on success. Use NextAuth.js with credentials provider storing users in a local JSON file or lightweight DB.
acceptance_criteria: Route /auth renders a page with both Login and Sign Up form tabs/toggles
Sign Up form has fields: name, email, password, confirm password
Login form has fields: email, password
Client-side validation: email format, password min 8 chars, passwords match on signup
On successful login, user is redirected to /dashboard
On failed login, an error message is displayed inline
NextAuth session is established and accessible via useSession()
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Protected route middleware
userStories.description: Add Next.js middleware that redirects unauthenticated users to /auth when they try to access protected routes (/dashboard, /settings, /profile, /notifications).
acceptance_criteria: middleware.ts exists at the project root and exports a config with matcher for protected routes
Unauthenticated requests to /dashboard, /settings, /profile, /notifications redirect to /auth
Authenticated requests pass through normally
The /auth page itself is accessible without authentication
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Dashboard page with summary cards
userStories.description: Create a /dashboard page that displays summary cards showing placeholder stats (total users, active sessions, recent activity count, system status). Layout uses a responsive CSS grid.
acceptance_criteria: Route /dashboard renders a page with at least 4 summary stat cards
Each card displays a title, a numeric value, and a subtle icon or indicator
Cards are arranged in a responsive grid (2 cols on mobile, 4 on desktop)
Page is only accessible when authenticated (redirects to /auth otherwise)
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: User profile page
userStories.description: Create a /profile page that displays the current user's information (name, email, member since date) and allows editing the display name.
acceptance_criteria: Route /profile renders with the authenticated user's name, email, and join date
An 'Edit' button reveals an inline form to change the display name
Submitting the form calls PUT /api/user/profile and updates the displayed name
A success toast/message appears after saving
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: User API routes (CRUD)
userStories.description: Create API routes under /api/user for getting and updating the current user's profile data. Data is stored in a local JSON file or lightweight store.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/user/profile returns the authenticated user's profile as JSON
PUT /api/user/profile accepts {name} in the body and updates the stored user
Both endpoints return 401 if the request is not authenticated
Response shapes are typed with TypeScript interfaces
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Dark mode toggle with persistence
userStories.description: Add a dark/light mode toggle accessible from the site header. The preference persists in localStorage and respects the system preference as default.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle button in the header switches between dark and light themes
Theme applies a 'dark' class to the <html> element (Tailwind dark mode strategy)
Preference is saved to localStorage under key 'theme'
On first visit with no saved preference, the system preference (prefers-color-scheme) is used
Page does not flash the wrong theme on reload (use a blocking script or cookie approach)
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Search with command palette
userStories.description: Add a global search/command palette (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) that searches across page names and navigates to the selected result.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K on Mac) opens a centered modal/dialog
The dialog has a text input that filters a list of navigable pages in real time
Selecting a result navigates to that page and closes the dialog
Pressing Escape closes the dialog
The component is accessible (focus trapped in dialog, aria attributes present)
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Settings page with notification preferences
userStories.description: Create a /settings page where users can toggle notification preferences (email notifications on/off, in-app notifications on/off) and save them.
acceptance_criteria: Route /settings renders a form with toggle switches for email and in-app notifications
Current preferences are loaded from GET /api/user/settings on mount
Toggling and clicking Save calls PUT /api/user/settings with the new values
A success message confirms the save
GET and PUT /api/user/settings endpoints exist and return/accept {emailNotifications: bool, inAppNotifications: bool}
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors

userStories.title: Notifications dropdown
userStories.description: Add a notifications bell icon in the header that opens a dropdown showing recent notifications (placeholder data). Include a /notifications page listing all notifications.
acceptance_criteria: A bell icon in the header shows an unread count badge when there are unread notifications
Clicking the bell opens a dropdown with the 5 most recent notifications
Each notification shows a title, message preview, and relative timestamp
A 'View all' link in the dropdown navigates to /notifications
The /notifications page lists all notifications with read/unread styling
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors
